author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Rebuild EmuCoreX library metadata without replacing save data
summary: Distinguish covers and title cache from game images, profiles, memory cards, and states; back up the durable layers; refresh only metadata; and compare hashes before considering broader data resets.
heroAlt: PCSX2 Qt application window showing a populated game list whose presentation metadata can be rebuilt separately from saves

blocks.text: Name the missing layer before clearing anything

A blank cover, stale title, missing description, unavailable image path, absent profile, and missing memory-card save are different faults. Metadata refresh should affect presentation records, not the verified game image or emulator-data layers that contain progress. Start by opening the game entry and confirming its serial and file path; if the file itself is unavailable, repair storage access first.
Do not use Android Clear storage or delete the emulator-data folder to repair artwork. Those actions can remove durable configuration and saves that a metadata refresh never needed to touch.
Snapshot durable data and current identity

items: Memory-card and profile backups created while emulation is closed.
Game image path, serial, region, and SHA-256 recorded for two affected entries.
A screenshot of favorites and any custom labels.
Stable internet access only if the metadata source requires it.
Knowledge of the app's normal Refresh or metadata action for the current build.

blocks.text: Refresh presentation records at the smallest scope

items: 1. Cold-boot one affected game to prove the image and BIOS still work before metadata maintenance.
2. Return to the library and run the normal refresh once, waiting for scanning and metadata activity to settle.
3. Inspect the same entry for unchanged path, serial, region, and favorite state.
4. If the build exposes a cover or metadata-specific retry, use it on one item before refreshing the entire catalog.
5. Force-stop and reopen EmuCoreX to confirm the repaired presentation persists.
6. Open the per-game profile and native memory-card save for the test title.
7. Hash the backed-up and active memory-card files only after closing emulation; they should be unchanged by presentation repair.

blocks.text: Artwork can remain unavailable because a remote source has no match for that serial, because network or locale lookup failed, or because cached presentation data is stale. A correct fallback title with no cover is safer than attaching another game's metadata to a working image.
Prove metadata changed and durable data did not
The evidence should show a presentation fix with stable identity and saves.

items: Game path, serial, region, and image hash remain the same.
Favorite and per-game profile remain attached to the intended entry.
Native save loads after full boot.
Memory-card hash is unchanged when no game save was written.
Another unaffected library entry retains its metadata.

blocks.text: Do not call these metadata problems

items: Folder is unavailable: repair Android permission or mount state.
Serial changes between scans: verify image identity and duplicate roots.
Game boots under the wrong edition: metadata cannot correct a bad or mislabeled working copy.
Memory-card file is missing: restore the data layer rather than refreshing covers.

blocks.text: Restore the presentation snapshot only if needed

If refresh makes labels worse, preserve the new state for diagnosis, restore the previous metadata or app-supported cache backup when available, and keep the game files and emulator-data backup untouched. Reattach a manual label only after serial identity is certain.
Remote metadata can be incomplete without being corrupt
Regional and revision-specific entries may not have the same artwork coverage. Do not merge them or substitute metadata purely for visual consistency. Identity is more important than a filled card.
